facts.fact: Central Bank of Liberia Governor Henry Saamoi said the bank launched the Pay Na-Na platform in December 2025, which has carried transactions, with mobile money operators engaged and banks and fintechs still being onboarded.

LBR.note: Document states nothing on consumer rules or redress; a pledge to engage providers on P2P charges is not a rule.
Document states nothing on cross-border payments.

facts.fact: Central Bank of Liberia Governor Henry Saamoi said government-to-person payments were the first use case of the Pay Na-Na platform launched in December 2025, so citizens receive government payments digitally.

LBR.note: No survey figure on account holding.

facts.fact: Central Bank of Liberia Governor Henry Saamoi said Pay Na-Na, launched in December 2025, has begun with mobile money operators and records transactions, while full interoperability across mobile money networks and banks is still a priority, with banks and fintechs to be onboarded.

LBR.note: Document states nothing on tax or fee payment.
A financial-literacy curriculum for elementary schools is not internet in secondary schools or a compulsory digital subject.
